answer.rationale:
The tempting read of memory is that memory_c2 already proved the low-cost switch works, so switching primary now satisfies the 18% mandate in one move. I want that record pulled before relying on it, because its success criteria are cost and invoicing accuracy — not quality escapes, not on-time delivery against a committed volume line. A switch that looks optimal on the measured metric (unit cost) can quietly degrade the unmeasured ones (line continuity, defect rate, supplier responsiveness), and at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer there is nowhere to absorb that. It also does not say whether the switched part was critical, single-sourced, or comparable in volume to this one. memory_c6 is the basis for what I actually intend, so it gets the second slot: I need to know whether the volume-pricing-for-term trade was won on this component class, and whether the longer term foreclosed later dual-sourcing.

The binding constraint is that the primary contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew. Letting it lapse converts delivery risk from uncertain to certain, which fails the stated objective outright — so add_second_source, which memory_c3 supports on its merits, cannot be the single action this cycle; it leaves no primary. Qualifying an unproven vendor as sole primary inside 14 days with no buffer is the same problem in reverse. That leaves the incumbent, and the incumbent has refused to reopen price — but price is not the only lever. memory_c4 and memory_c6 both point at levers that were not refused: benchmarked payment terms, and term length traded for volume pricing. I intend to negotiate on those, deliberately as a short bridge rather than a multi-year lock, so that next cycle can dual-source the low-cost vendor from a qualified position instead of a forced one.

Uncertainty I am not resolving: this likely does not reach 18% on its own. I would rather book a partial, verifiable cut with continuity intact and flag the shortfall to finance than take the full number on a single unreplicated switch precedent whose quality and delivery performance were never measured. If the archive shows memory_c2's switch was a critical high-volume part with tracked delivery and quality performance, and memory_c6 shows the term trade is exhausted here, I would revisit toward a phased switch.
